title: OOP Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Object-Oriented Programming lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Objects hold related facts
entries.summary: An object keeps related values together. A property is one named value inside the object.
notes: Put text values in quotes. Property names and values have different jobs.

entries.name: Methods perform actions
entries.summary: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it.

example.code:
const book = { title: "Moon", describe() { return this.title + " book"; } };
console.log(book.describe());

notes: An arrow function does not create its own this value. Use the method form shown here.

entries.name: Classes are plans
entries.summary: A class is a plan for making similar objects. Each object made from it is called an instance.
notes: Call this class with new; it is not an ordinary function call.

entries.name: Independent instances
entries.summary: Each instance has its own properties. Changing one book does not change a different book.
notes: Assigning b = a would make both names refer to the same object.

entries.name: Constructors set a starting state
entries.summary: A constructor sets up a new object. A default value is used when the caller leaves out an argument.
notes: Validate inputs when real callers might pass wrong kinds of values.

entries.name: Keeping data private
entries.summary: A private field starts with #. Code outside the class cannot directly read or change it.
notes: Private fields help organise access; they do not turn browser data into a secure online account.

entries.name: Getters provide a value
entries.summary: A getter calculates a value when you read a property. You do not call it with parentheses.
notes: Read .area, not .area(), because this member is a getter.

entries.name: Inheritance adds to a class
entries.summary: Inheritance lets one class extend another. The child class receives methods from its parent.
notes: Use inheritance only when the child really is a kind of the parent.

entries.name: Overriding a method
entries.summary: A child can replace an inherited method with its own version. This is called overriding.
notes: Keep the method purpose clear when replacing it in a child.

entries.name: Polymorphism uses one common action
entries.summary: Polymorphism means different objects can answer the same method call. The caller uses the action without choosing each object type.
notes: Each object in this list must provide speak before you call it.

entries.name: Composition builds from parts
entries.summary: Composition gives an object another object to use. A bike has a bell; a bike is not a kind of bell.
notes: Do not make Bike extend Bell just to borrow ring.

entries.name: Give each class a clear job
entries.summary: A class is easier to understand when it has one clear job. A basket can add prices without also drawing the whole web page.
notes: A class with many unrelated jobs becomes hard to change and test.
